titulo.texto: Zoomorphic Vessel in the Shape of a Fish

frase_gancho.texto: A clay fish that carries the lake to the table and to the tomb.

puente_narrativo.texto: From the waters of the valley we move on to long journeys. Walk to the Priest of Atlihuayan: he comes from Morelos and bears a style that speaks of another world, that of the Olmec.

guion_corto.texto: This vessel of polished black clay is shaped like a fish. The round belly serves as the container, the open mouth is the spout, and sunken circles mark the eyes. With a few incised lines, the fins, the tail, and the edge of the scales are drawn, and it still bears traces of red paint. It came from the tomb of a young adult, among the offerings that accompanied him. It is the same lake of the ducks, seen from below: fish, frogs, and aquatic plants fed the village, and that is why they appear in its art. It is a sober, almost geometric piece, and that is why it looks so modern.

guion_largo.texto:
In the lakes of the Valley of Mexico there was much more than water. There were charales and other tiny fish, acociles, frogs, axolotls, turtles, aquatic insects, and edible plants, and the villagers of three thousand years ago knew how to make use of them. Clay weights for nets and other fishing tools have been found in lakeside villages, and even today charales and acociles are sold in the city’s markets. This vessel is a tribute to that world.

Notice how it is resolved. It follows the same logic as the duck you just saw, but more austere. The body of the fish is the body of the vessel, and the artist added only what was essential: sunken circles for the eyes, an open mouth for filling and emptying, and incised lines for the fins, the tail, and the scales. Nothing is superfluous. If the duck was elegant, the fish is almost geometric, and that is why, three thousand years later, it looks so contemporary.

A piece like this was not made for daily use. It appeared in a tomb, among the offerings of a young adult, about thirty years old. Here is an idea worth pausing over. Many Mesoamerican peoples believed that what lay beneath the earth and what lay beneath the water were connected. Springs were mouths of the underworld, and the lagoon, a doorway. Placing a fish beside a dead person was not decoration: it was giving them a traveling companion through that world of water.

That idea had a very long life. In the Teotihuacán Hall you will see a mural with a paradise of water, Tlalocan, the place where those who died by water or by lightning went. There, people swim, sing, play, and gather fruit beside water that never runs out. The Tlatilco vessel is a distant ancestor of that mural: century after century, the people of the valley imagined the afterlife as a place that was damp, green, and full of life.

The color red also deserves a comment. Many Tlatilco vessels preserve traces of red pigment, which was applied to the clay and to the bodies of the deceased. Red was the color of blood and of life, and in tombs it was a way of sending the dead off with energy for the road. If you look closely, traces still remain in the grooves of the incisions.

If you compare it with [the Acrobat](mna_s03_acrobata_tlatilco), you will notice something curious: in both pieces the opening of the vessel is a part of the body, a knee in one case, a mouth in the other. The potters of Tlatilco liked the useful and the expressive to be one and the same thing.

And one last detail, to connect with the rest of the hall. Notice how many aquatic animals there are in the art of this village: ducks, fish, frogs, turtles. There are very few animals of the mountains or the open sky. That tells us where their imagination lived: at water level. Further on, when you reach the Mexica Hall, remember this lake: it was still there, three thousand years later, and the great capital rose in the middle of it.

texto: Look for the sunken circles that form the fish’s eyes
Follow the incised lines of the fins and the tail
Find traces of red paint in the grooves of the clay

texto.Material: Polished black ceramic with incisions and traces of red cinnabar pigment
texto.Dimensions: 14 cm high x 26.2 cm long x 15.5 cm in diameter

texto.pregunta: Myth: This vessel is a toy or a garden ornament.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It is a funerary offering: it came from a tomb and accompanied a deceased person, perhaps as a traveling companion in a world linked to water.
